templates.name: Addition/similarity: a further item of the same kind
Contrast: established view or appearance, then a finding that breaks it
Contrast: positive claim, then a limiting fact about the same subject
Cause/effect: condition, principle or evidence, then its consequence
Cause/effect: need or judgment, then the action it motivates
Concession: supported claim, then a fact that qualifies it
Emphasis: stronger same-direction fact (content-contrast trap at hard)
Purpose and aptness: goal then deliberate act, or a fitting echo
Specification/restatement: exact content or plain rewording
Sequence/time: next step, earlier or later event, end of a long effort
Example: general claim, then one named instance

items.passage: The Pompeii worm, which inhabits tubes on hydrothermal vent chimneys in the eastern Pacific, is frequently described as the most heat-tolerant complex animal on Earth. Temperatures approaching 80°C have been recorded at the base of its tube. ______ when researchers maintained specimens in pressurized aquariums, the worms tolerated water of about 42°C, and those exposed to 50°C sustained tissue damage.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first two sentences give the worm’s reputation as the most heat-tolerant complex animal and the support for it: temperatures approaching 80°C at the base of its tube. The aquarium results limit that claim: the worms tolerated about 42°C but suffered tissue damage at 50°C, far below 80°C. “That said” marks this qualification of a claim the passage has just supported.

A.why_wrong: The worm’s reputation and the 80°C reading do not cause the worms to tolerate 42°C or to be harmed at 50°C; the aquarium results cut against the reputation.

B.why_wrong: The aquarium results are not a particular case of the worm’s heat tolerance; they show limits well below the 80°C behind its reputation.

C.why_wrong: Water of about 42°C sounds hot, but damage at 50°C is not further evidence of extreme heat tolerance; it works against the claim built on the 80°C reading.

items.notes: K2 band 7 on the ecb31049 move (a reputation, then a record that cuts against it), with the evidence for the claim placed just before the blank, so the qualifying fact must be linked back past it to the 80°C figure and the reputation. Facts from general knowledge; not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no invented names and no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.
band7_moves: the 80°C support sits in the sentence right before the blank, so the blank sentence reads at first as more temperature data about the same worm
the limitation shows only once 42°C and 50°C are set against the 80°C reading behind the reputation; no contrast word inside the blank sentence carries the turn
Additionally pulls because tolerating 42°C still sounds impressive; In particular pulls because the sentence gives exact temperatures; Hence pulls on the research being prompted by the reputation
key outside the core 13; decoy set differs from ecb31049 (Hence, In particular, Additionally); no In fact or Indeed on offer, no contrast decoy
register 5.48 chars per word, so the item passes gate 4 of band7/transitions.md section 6 (a concession key fails proxy 3 by construction, as ecb31049 does)

fixes: explanation: 'The first sentence gives' to 'The first two sentences give' (the 80°C support is sentence 2)
review.notes: No fact check (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16). Attribution check: no made-up finding is attributed to a real, named person or organisation; named people, works and places carry commonly known facts, and findings go to unnamed researchers or 'a study'. Second-sense check: No In fact or Indeed beside the qualification key. Hence fails against both earlier sentences (neither the reputation nor the 80°C reading yields a 42°C limit); In particular fails (the aquarium figures are no detail of the 80°C reading); Additionally fails (42°C and damage at 50°C cut against the claim, they do not add to it). rw_options: no second acceptable connective.

band7.why: Mirrors ecb31049 move for move: a reputation and its support, then a record that cuts against it, keyed That said with cause, additive and specification decoys (Hence, Additionally, In particular for For this reason, Moreover, Specifically). The support (80°C) sits right before the blank, so the turn shows only once 42°C and 50°C are set back against it; key outside the core 13, no obvious decoy, register 5.48 passes gate 4. Caveat: 'sustained tissue damage' is a turn cue inside B, as 'no ... had ever generated' is in ecb31049, and K2 sits close to band 6 (band7/transitions.md section 5).

items.passage: Mozambican novelist Mia Couto, whose first book appeared in 1983, writes in Portuguese, the language of his country’s former colonizer. Critics often describe him as reinventing that language from within. ______ rather than abandoning Portuguese for an African language, as some African writers have done, he reshapes it, coining new words and adapting his sentences to the rhythms of Mozambican speech.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence reports an abstract claim: critics say Couto reinvents Portuguese “from within.” The next sentence spells out what that means in plain terms: he keeps Portuguese but reshapes it, coining words and following Mozambican speech rhythms. “That is” signals this restatement.

A.why_wrong: The critics’ description does not cause Couto’s way of writing; the sentence explains what the description means.

C.why_wrong: The sentence is not a separate point about Couto; coining words and reshaping the language are what “reinventing that language from within” refers to.

D.why_wrong: The contrast with writers who abandoned Portuguese sits inside the sentence; the sentence as a whole agrees with, and restates, the critics’ view in the first sentence.

items.notes: Restating an abstract claim (3.1 pattern) without 3.1's debate frame; the rather-than clause inside B pulls toward In contrast. Facts from general knowledge; not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no invented names and no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

fixes: explanation: the critics’ claim is in the second sentence, not the first
review.notes: No fact check (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16). Attribution check: no made-up finding is attributed to a real, named person or organisation; named people, works and places carry commonly known facts, and findings go to unnamed researchers or 'a study'. Second-sense check: In contrast fails against every clause: B agrees with Couto writing in Portuguese and with the critics; the contrast with other writers sits inside B. Consequently fails (neither Portuguese being the colonizer’s language nor the critics’ view causes his practice); Moreover fails (B spells out 'reinventing from within', no separate point). rw_options: no second acceptable connective.

band7.why: band_target 6 (plan). That is restating an abstract claim, the e3edc138 frame (band 6), with the rather-than clause inside B pulling In contrast; S1’s band-7 form is the frequency key (d3b7d7a3), not used here.

items.passage: Tides rise and fall on schedules that can be predicted years in advance, making them an attractive source of renewable energy. Yet tidal power remains a marginal contributor to global electricity generation. ______ the world’s largest tidal power station, South Korea’s Sihwa Lake facility, has a capacity of 254 megawatts, less than a third of that of a single large nuclear reactor.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence claims that tidal power remains marginal. The next sentence strengthens that claim: even the world’s largest tidal station has less than a third of the capacity of one large nuclear reactor. “In fact” introduces this stronger supporting fact.

A.why_wrong: Naming the largest station looks like a point against “marginal,” but its small capacity supports the claim rather than qualifying it.

B.why_wrong: The station’s small capacity does not hold true in spite of tidal power being marginal; it is evidence that tidal power is marginal.

D.why_wrong: The station’s capacity is not a separate point; it is the strongest evidence for the claim that tidal power remains marginal.

items.notes: M1 band 7 varied from the five existing M1 hard items, which all run the extreme-value-then-typical-value frame. Facts from general knowledge; not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no invented names and no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.
band7_moves: surface contrast with a supporting relation (00e0170f shape, not the outlier-then-majority frame): the blank sentence opens on ‘the world’s largest tidal power station’, which reads at first as a counterexample to ‘marginal’
the support is visible only once the 254-megawatt figure is set against a single nuclear reactor and linked back to ‘marginal’

That said and Nevertheless (a synonym pair, as in 00e0170f) both fit a first-pass misreading of ‘the world’s largest tidal power station’ as a concession to ‘marginal’; Additionally pulls on the new figure

key outside the core 13; no example or specification decoy (either could read as illustrating the claim) and no cause decoy (Consequently was dropped in review: little deployment, so even the biggest station is small, is an arguable reading)

fixes: explanation: the 'marginal' claim is in the second sentence, not the first
review.notes: No fact check (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16). Attribution check: no made-up finding is attributed to a real, named person or organisation; named people, works and places carry commonly known facts, and findings go to unnamed researchers or 'a study'. Second-sense check: Writer’s request: In fact is unambiguously emphatic. A corrective In fact needs B to overturn the sentence before it, but 'less than a third of that of a single large nuclear reactor' confirms 'marginal'; sentence 1’s 'attractive' was already turned by 'Yet', so no clause is left for In fact to correct. That said and Nevertheless fail on the same clause (B supports 'marginal') and against sentence 1 (turning back to 'attractive' would need a large figure, and B frames 254 MW as small). Additionally fails as in a266d876 (B is evidence for 'marginal', not a separate point). rw_options: no second acceptable connective.

band7.why: 00e0170f shape: a goal or promise left marginal, then In fact with the extreme case that proves it, offered beside the same adversative synonym pair (That said, Nevertheless) and an additive decoy as in a266d876. The blank sentence opens on 'the world’s largest tidal power station', which reads first as a counterexample, so the surface points the wrong way. Gate: key outside the core 13, no obvious decoy; register 5.15 is under 5.3, but the surface-contrast proxy passes ('Yet' in the sentence before the blank, adversative decoys on offer). Not the outlier-then-majority frame of the other M1 hard items.

items.passage: The concrete artists of São Paulo treated a painting as an objective arrangement of geometric forms, planned with mathematical precision and free of personal expression. ______ the Rio de Janeiro artists behind the 1959 Neo-Concrete Manifesto, though also working with geometric forms, insisted that art should engage the viewer’s senses and emotions.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The passage compares two groups of Brazilian artists. The São Paulo concrete artists made impersonal, mathematically planned works, while the Rio artists, though also geometric, wanted art to engage the viewer’s senses and emotions. “By contrast” marks these opposing views.

B.why_wrong: Both groups used geometric forms, but the Rio artists rejected the São Paulo artists’ impersonal, mathematical approach; their views are opposed, not similar.

C.why_wrong: The Rio artists are not an instance of the São Paulo concrete artists; they held the opposing view of what geometric art should do.

D.why_wrong: The sentence does not add a further point about the São Paulo artists; it describes a second group with an opposing view.

items.notes: Plan cell asked for band 7, but C1_two_subject has no band-7 official items (spec/rw/band7/transitions.md section 5), so this is a strong band 6 with band_target 6 (WAVE.md). items.passage: Most bony fishes propel themselves by sweeping a caudal fin, or tail fin, from side to side. The ocean sunfish, ______ possesses no true caudal fin: its body terminates abruptly in a clavus, a stiff, rudderlike structure, and the animal generates thrust by flapping its elongated dorsal and anal fins.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence says most bony fishes swim with a tail fin. The ocean sunfish has no true tail fin and swims with other fins instead. “In contrast” marks this difference between the sunfish and most bony fishes.

A.why_wrong: The sunfish is not an example of fishes that swim with a tail fin; it lacks one.

B.why_wrong: How most bony fishes swim does not cause the sunfish to lack a tail fin.

D.why_wrong: The sunfish does not swim the way most bony fishes do; it is the exception.

items.notes: Interrupter after the subject (2.6 position). Facts from general knowledge; not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no invented names and no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: The Islamic calendar is purely lunar: its twelve months total roughly 354 days, so they migrate gradually through the seasons, and Ramadan begins approximately eleven days earlier each year. ______ the Hebrew calendar, though also governed by lunar phases, periodically inserts an additional month, keeping each holiday within approximately the same season.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The Islamic calendar’s months drift through the seasons. The Hebrew calendar, although it also follows the Moon, adds an extra month so that its holidays stay in about the same season. “By contrast” marks this difference between the two calendars.

B.why_wrong: Both calendars follow the Moon, but the Hebrew calendar keeps its holidays in the same season while the Islamic calendar’s months drift, so they are not alike in the respect the passage discusses.

C.why_wrong: The Hebrew calendar is not an example of the purely lunar Islamic calendar; it adds months that the Islamic calendar does not.

D.why_wrong: The sentence does not reword the point about the Islamic calendar; it describes a different calendar that works differently.

items.notes: Two calendars, one attribute (drift through the seasons), opposite values; the though-also clause pulls toward Similarly. No cause decoy: lunar drift is the general reason lunisolar calendars add a month, so For this reason could look acceptable. Sentence-initial By contrast after a long first sentence (2.18 position). Facts from general knowledge; not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no invented names and no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

review.notes: No fact check (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16). Attribution check: no made-up finding is attributed to a real, named person or organisation; named people, works and places carry commonly known facts, and findings go to unnamed researchers or 'a study'. Second-sense check: Similarly fails: 'though also governed by lunar phases' is subordinate, and the main clause keeps holidays in season, the opposite of drifting. For instance and In other words fail (a different calendar). No cause decoy (writer’s choice, right: drift is why lunisolar calendars add a month). rw_options: no second acceptable connective.

items.passage: Russian thistle, the source of most tumbleweeds in the American West, reached South Dakota in the 1870s, probably in a shipment of contaminated flax seed. After windstorms, the detached plants accumulate against fences and obstruct highways. ______ the tumbleweeds are highly flammable, and when they burn, they can carry wildfires across firebreaks.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence names one problem the tumbleweeds cause: they pile up against fences and block highways. The last sentence adds a second, separate problem: they burn easily and can spread wildfires. “In addition” adds this further problem.

A.why_wrong: The fire danger does not hold true in spite of the plants piling up on fences and highways; it is a second problem of the same kind.

C.why_wrong: Flammability is not an example of the plants piling against fences and blocking highways; it is a separate problem.

D.why_wrong: The fire danger is new information, not a rewording of the point about fences and highways.

items.notes: A further harm of the same kind (2.10 pattern). Key In addition and a decoy set unlike w2b3_07 (Moreover). No cause decoy: an earlier draft called the plants dried, which made Thus (dried, so flammable) look acceptable. Facts from general knowledge; not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no invented names and no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: In 2019, a team of geographers in Chile set out to measure how unevenly the shade cast by street trees is distributed among neighborhoods of Santiago with different household incomes. ______ the researchers calculated the share of each neighborhood’s sidewalks covered by tree canopy at midday in summer and then compared those figures across wealthy and low-income districts.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence states the team’s general aim: measuring how unevenly street-tree shade is spread across neighborhoods with different incomes. The next sentence gives the exact method: the share of sidewalk under tree canopy, compared between rich and poor districts. “Specifically” introduces these precise details.

A.why_wrong: The sentence does not hold true in spite of the team’s aim; it spells out how the team carried out that aim.

B.why_wrong: Calculating canopy cover is not a separate point added to the team’s aim; it is how the team measured the uneven distribution of shade.

C.why_wrong: The calculation did not come before the team set out to measure shade; it is the method the team used to do so.

items.passage: Music for the guqin, a seven-string Chinese zither, has traditionally been notated in a tablature that is prescriptive rather than descriptive; ______ the notation specifies which string to pluck, which finger to employ, and where to press the string, but not how the resulting melody should sound. Rhythm, in particular, is left largely to the performer’s interpretation.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first clause uses technical terms: the tablature is “prescriptive rather than descriptive.” The clause after the blank says the same thing plainly: it tells players what actions to perform, not what the music sounds like. “In other words” signals this rewording.

B.why_wrong: Telling players what to do rather than how the music sounds does not go against the notation being prescriptive; it is what prescriptive means here.

C.why_wrong: The clause does not describe a similar notation; it explains the guqin tablature itself.

D.why_wrong: The clause adds no separate feature of the notation; it restates “prescriptive rather than descriptive” in plain words.

items.notes: Technical phrase reworded after a semicolon; the but-not clause in B pulls toward nevertheless. Facts from general knowledge; not web-checked (Transitions, brief of 2026-10-16); no invented names and no made-up finding attributed to a real person or organisation.

items.passage: Because most of its vocabulary comes from English, Tok Pisin, a national language of Papua New Guinea, was long dismissed by outsiders as broken English. Linguists, ______ have documented its consistent grammar, which even marks distinctions that English lacks, such as separate words for “we” including the listener (yumi) and excluding the listener (mipela).
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence gives an old view of Tok Pisin: that it was merely broken English. Linguists have found the opposite: a consistent grammar with distinctions English does not make. “However” marks this turn from the old view to the finding.

A.why_wrong: The linguists are not an example of the outsiders who dismissed Tok Pisin; their findings go against that view.

B.why_wrong: The outsiders’ dismissal does not lead to the linguists’ findings; the findings contradict it.

D.why_wrong: The linguists’ findings do not add to the view of Tok Pisin as broken English; they overturn it.

items.passage: Antlion larvae excavate cone-shaped pits in loose sand and lie concealed at the bottom, awaiting passing insects. Each pit’s walls are constructed at the angle of repose: the steepest inclination at which granular material remains stable. ______ an ant that ventures onto the slope triggers a miniature avalanche that carries it toward the larva’s waiting mandibles.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The walls of the pit are as steep as loose sand can be, so they are on the edge of collapsing. Because of this, an ant’s step makes the sand slide and carries the ant down to the larva. “Consequently” marks this result.

A.why_wrong: The ant’s fall is not a rewording of the point about the angle of the walls; it is what happens because of that angle.

C.why_wrong: The ant’s fall is not an instance of the walls being shaped to the angle of repose; it is a result of it.

D.why_wrong: The sentence does not describe something similar to the shaping of the walls; it describes what the steep walls cause.
